claims.text: Controlled post-deposition annealing in forming gas at approximately 500°C for 30–120 minutes induces enhanced residual compressive stress in CoCrFeMnNi multilayer coatings.
The prescribed annealing can enhance compressive stress without causing significant phase transformations, grain growth, interface changes, or other microstructural changes.
Residual compressive stresses oppose externally applied tensile stresses.
Opposition from residual compressive stress reduces the effective stress available for dislocation activation.
Reduced effective stress delays dislocation activation and motion.
Delayed dislocation activation and motion diminish the rate of time-dependent plastic deformation.
Annealed coatings with enhanced residual compressive stress will exhibit significantly lower creep rates than as-deposited controls under otherwise identical conditions.
Creep-rate reduction will correlate with the magnitude of induced residual compressive stress.
The proposed behavior applies near 500°C and annealing durations of 30–120 minutes provided significant microstructural changes do not occur.
Minor grain coarsening or interface changes could also contribute to any observed creep resistance.
